tasks.short: Decide a referral is needed, find the right provider, discuss it with the client, consult the GP or provider, write the referral letter and send it securely.

steps.what: Speech therapist decides the client needs additional medical or educational services
Speech therapist looks up which providers handle the problem nearby
Speech therapist discusses the referral with the client and family
Speech therapist consults the GP or the receiving provider by phone
Speech therapist writes the referral letter to refer clients
Speech therapist checks the final referral letter: the question, findings and goals match the record and what was agreed with the client, and it goes to the chosen provider
Speech therapist sends the checked referral letter: by post today, by one release as secure mail after the change

tasks.design: A regional provider list ({OTHER}) shared by local practices shows who treats what and their waiting times. A referral template in the patient record fills client details, test results and goals, and the therapist writes the question; the therapist checks the letter and releases it by secure mail. Deciding, discussing and consulting stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Providers were found through personal contacts, and letters written and posted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems fill referral templates and send them by secure mail.
tasks.still_hard: Waiting lists change fast; the list goes stale without upkeep.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which colleague will take a complicated child sooner.

reach.learn: Whether structured letters cut questions back.

evidence.claim: Record systems fill referral templates and send them by secure mail.
Health data are special category data and must be sent securely.

assumptions: Boundary: from findings to the referral sent; the receiving provider's intake is outside.
Input contract: provider list kept by the regional practices' network; fallback is personal contacts.
Deciding, discussing and consulting do not change.
Providers' time is outside the therapist's savings.
s2 keeps 60 for reading the provider list and choosing; s5 keeps 65 because the question to the provider is written by the therapist; s6 keeps 10 for the release.

already_counted.description: Speech therapist checks the filled letter.

incremental.description: Speech therapist updates the shared provider list.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter exactly as checked by the therapist in s5b, sent once by secure mail to the chosen provider; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the provider list is incomplete, so s2 keeps 90, and the template fills little, so s5 keeps 85 (7.8); high: list and template as designed (14.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess communication needs, try alternative communication devices with the client, build the vocabulary pages, apply to the insurer for funding and train family and carers.

steps.what: Speech therapist assesses the client's needs for alternative communication
Speech therapist tries alternative communication devices and strategies with the client
Speech therapist builds the vocabulary and symbol pages on the device
Speech therapist writes the funding application for the insurer
Speech therapist checks the final funding application: the needs, the device and the reasons match the assessment, and it goes to the client's insurer
Speech therapist sends the checked application to the insurer: by post today, by one release on the insurer's portal after the change
Speech therapist trains family and carers to use the device

tasks.design: Communication devices start from a core vocabulary set ({OTHER}), so the therapist adds personal words and photos instead of building every page. The funding application fills from the assessment in the patient record, and the therapist checks it and releases it on the insurer's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}). Assessing, trying devices and training carers stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vocabulary pages were built one by one and applications written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Communication devices come with core vocabulary sets, and record systems fill application forms.
tasks.still_hard: Each client's words and symbols are personal; core sets are only a start.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one word a child most wants to say.

reach.learn: Whether shared setups speed up device use.

evidence.claim: Communication devices come with core vocabulary sets that can be personalised.
Health insurers can fund communication aids after an application with a professional's assessment.

assumptions: Boundary: from referral to trained carers; device repairs are outside.
Input contract: assessment results in the patient record; insurer's form requirements; fallback is writing by hand.
Assessing, trying devices and training do not change.
Insurers' time is outside the therapist's savings.
s3 keeps 60 for adding personal words and photos. s4 keeps 60 because the reasons for the device are written by the therapist; s5 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Does time to first use of the device fall?

already_counted.description: Speech therapist checks the filled application.

incremental.description: Speech therapist keeps core vocabulary sets current.

approvals.approved_version: The funding application exactly as checked by the therapist in s4b, submitted once on the client's insurer's portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the insurer's form needs mostly free text, so s4 keeps 85, and core sets fit few clients, so s3 keeps 80 (9.3); high: form and core sets as designed (15.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pick courses and conferences with register points, attend them, send certificates to the register, write up research results, format references and present.

steps.what: Speech therapist picks conferences and courses that carry register points
Speech therapist participates in conferences, training and continuing education courses
Course providers report the therapist's attendance to the quality register
Speech therapist checks each certificate a provider did not report: right event, date, points and own registration number
Speech therapist uploads certificates to the quality register: every certificate today; after the change only for providers that do not report
Speech therapist writes up research results on new treatment methods
Speech therapist checks references and formats the manuscript to the journal's rules
Speech therapist presents the findings at a conference

tasks.design: The quality register's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}) lists accredited courses with points and takes attendance from providers directly. A reference manager formats citations to the journal's style and checks them against library records. Attending, writing and presenting stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses were searched for one by one, certificates uploaded by hand and references formatted manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Quality registers list accredited courses, and reference managers format citations.
tasks.still_hard: Writing up research takes the therapist's own thinking.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to colleagues why a new method worked for these clients.

reach.learn: Whether register lists help plan training.

evidence.claim: Quality registers list accredited courses and record points from providers.
Registered therapists must collect points each period to stay in the quality register.

assumptions: Boundary: from register requirements to presented findings; journal peer review is outside.
Input contract: course lists and points from the quality register; fallback is uploading by hand.
Attending, writing and presenting do not change.

Providers that do not report need a manual upload (s3 keeps 25); the providers' reports (s2b, share 1) are outside the therapist's savings. s5 keeps 40 for checking references the manager cannot match.

incremental.description: Speech therapist keeps the reference library and journal styles current.

approvals.approved_version: The certificate with event, date and points exactly as checked by the therapist in s2c, uploaded once to the therapist's own file in the quality register; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few providers report attendance, so s3 keeps 100, and many references need manual fixes, so s5 keeps 70 (6.7); high: most providers report and the reference manager works as designed (12.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run computer-based speech and language tests, score them against norms, interpret the results, measure voice with analysis software, set up practice apps and copy results into the record.

steps.what: Speech therapist runs computer applications to identify communication disabilities
Speech therapist scores the tests: by hand against norm tables today; after the change only paper-only tests are scored by hand
Speech therapist interprets the results
Speech therapist measures voice with speech-analysis software
Speech therapist sets up therapy apps that assist the client in home practice
Speech therapist copies test and voice results into the record: by hand today; after the change checks the exported values and copies paper-only results

tasks.design: Computer-based tests score responses against the published norm tables in the test software ({OTHER}) and export scores and voice measures to the patient record. Practice apps start from programme templates the therapist adjusts. Running tests, measuring voice and interpreting results stay with the therapist; no AI diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were looked up in norm tables and copied into the record by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Test software scores against norms and exports results.
tasks.still_hard: Some tests exist only on paper and are still scored by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a low score reflects fatigue, not a disorder.

reach.learn: Whether exported results speed up joint assessments.

evidence.claim: Computer-based language tests score responses against norm tables and export results.
Software with a diagnostic medical purpose may be a medical device; providers must know whether it is one.

assumptions: Boundary: from referral to results on file; treatment planning is outside.
Input contract: norm tables from the test publisher; fallback is scoring by hand.
Running tests and interpreting do not change.
Paper-only tests are scored by hand and copied in, so s2 and s6 keep 20 each, which includes checking exported values.

incremental.description: Speech therapist checks exported scores after software updates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the tests used are paper-only, so s2 and s6 keep 50 (18.0); high: most tests are computer-based (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The speech therapist keeps assessment, device trials, research and referral decisions; scoring, letters and applications by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who spends saved time on device training with families.
